info.name: local-mock-server — manual verification
info.description:
Three scenarios that exercise the design decisions behind this mock server.

Before you run, start the server from the project root:

npm run dev -- --spec examples/petstore.yaml --port 4010 --seed 42 --log-level silent

Each request carries assertions, so Run collection gives you pass/fail. The interesting part of every response is in the Headers tab, not only the body.

Folder C compares responses to each other and therefore depends on run order.

item.name: A1 - documented example is served verbatim

request.description: GET /pets/{petId} declares an examples map, so the payload comes from the document rather than the generator. Expect X-Mock-Payload: example and no X-Mock-Seed.

exec: pm.test('payload is an example, not generated', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Mock-Payload')).to.eql('example'); });
pm.test('no seed on an example payload', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Mock-Seed')).to.be.undefined; });
pm.test('body is the documented example', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().name).to.eql('Rex'); });

item.name: A2 - Prefer code=404 selects the documented 404

request.description: Prefer is the only control channel, so it can never collide with a query parameter the spec declares. This 404 is the one the specification documents.

exec: pm.test('served as plain JSON, not problem+json', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Content-Type')).to.include('application/json'); });
pm.test('body is the documented error example', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().code).to.eql('NOT_FOUND'); });

item.name: A3 - an undocumented route is the mock's own error

request.description: Same status as A2, different meaning. Distinguishable by X-Mock-Source, by Content-Type, and by the body code member - any one of the three is sufficient.

exec: pm.test('came from the mock itself', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Mock-Source')).to.eql('mock'); });
pm.test('body carries a mock error code', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().code).to.eql('ROUTE_NOT_FOUND'); });
pm.test('distinguishable from A2 by source alone', function () {

item.name: B1 - query parameter above its maximum

request.description: The spec declares limit with maximum 100. Expect 422 with a details array naming the parameter and the constraint it broke.

exec: pm.test('came from the mock itself', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Mock-Source')).to.eql('mock'); });
pm.test('details say what was wrong', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().details).to.be.an('array').that.is.not.empty; });

item.name: B2 - query parameter outside its enum

request.description: status is an enum of available, pending, sold.

exec: pm.test('details name the query parameter', function () { pm.expect(JSON.stringify(pm.response.json().details)).to.include('status'); });

item.name: B3 - a valid request still works (control)

request.description: Without this control it is impossible to tell strict validation from a broken endpoint.

exec: pm.test('body is a non-empty array of pets', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.be.an('array').that.is.not.empty; });

item.name: C. Determinism and seed scope (REQ-052, REQ-054)
C1 - generated payload, note the seed

request.description: GET /pets declares no example, so the payload is generated and carries the effective seed. With --seed 42 this should be 2220222242.

item.name: C2 - the same request repeats byte for byte

request.description: Identical to C1. The body must be identical too - this is the determinism guarantee.

exec: pm.test('C1 has been run', function () { pm.expect(seed, 'run C1 first').to.be.a('string').that.is.not.empty; });

item.name: C3 - a different request draws independently

request.description: Only the query string differs. The effective seed is derived from the request identity, so it must differ from C1. With --seed 42 this should be 2281214932.

exec: pm.test('C1 has been run', function () { pm.expect(seed, 'run C1 first').to.be.a('string').that.is.not.empty; });
